text:
Maya (Product Marketing): Quick alignment thread for the benchmark launch creative. Need a tight hero line, two chart variants (scatter + tail risk), and two micro-captions: one for self-serve engineers, one for platform buyers. Keep wording direct and testable.

Jon (Design): I'll run two visual treatments: 1) clean scatter (median latency vs $/1k tokens) with annotated levers (cache, quant), 2) stacked tail plots (50/95/99) with shaded SLA bands. Recommend single accent color for Redwood points.

Priya (Data): I'll provide the canonical CSV and a short methods note. Suggest we label cost axis in cents to avoid small decimals. Also include small badges for 'cache on' and 'dedicated'.

Ethan (Growth): Headline candidates: A) "Predictable latency. Predictable cost." B) "Faster responses. Lower unit cost." We'll A/B test them in hero + email. Email subject options ready.

Lena (DevRel): Micro-caption for engineers: "Engineers: use batching, prefix cache, and quantization to move down/right on the chart." Micro-caption for buyers: "Enterprises: Dedicated + smart routing reduces tail risk and preserves availability." Keep both under 20 words.

Maya (Product Marketing): Good. Priya please add a tiny sample CSV for Jon to use. Also include measurement note: GPU class, avg seq length, N requests.

Priya (Data): Sample rows: workload,variant,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_cents
chat,redwood-quant,42,180,1.2
chat,redwood-quant+cache,28,120,0.8
summarize,open-gt3,120,600,4.5
embed,embed-lite,18,40,0.6
I'll upload full CSV and methods blurb to the shared assets folder.

AssetsBot: New files uploaded to https://drive.redwood.dev/bench/1704728888 (scatter.png, tails.png, dataset.csv, methods.txt).

Jon (Design): Mockups uploaded. Ping here if copy needs tightening.

Maya (Product Marketing): Action items recap: Priya -> final CSV + methods; Jon -> polish charts with badges; Ethan -> set up A/B test UTMs; Lena -> finalize micro-captions. I'll assemble landing + email draft and circulate tomorrow AM. This thread is canonical for chart copy and annotations. :white_check_mark:
